members.name: regime_detection_vol_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 10 by liquidity)
members.thesis: A simplified Hidden Markov Model (HMM) with 2 states (low-vol / high-vol) fitted on rolling 120-bar 1-min return sequences can detect intraday volatility regime shifts 2-5 bars before simple threshold-based methods. The HMM captures the transition probability between regimes: when the model assigns
entry_long: low_to_high == True AND HMM_prob_high_vol > 0.80 AND EMA_8 > EMA_21 (vol expansion + upward momentum)
OR high_to_low == True AND HMM_prob_high_vol < 0.20 AND close < vwap (vol contraction + below VWAP mean rev)
entry_short: low_to_high == True AND HMM_prob_high_vol > 0.80 AND EMA_8 < EMA_21 (vol expansion + downward momentum)
OR high_to_low == True AND HMM_prob_high_vol < 0.20 AND close > vwap (vol contraction + above VWAP mean rev)
members.exit_target: low_to_high: 1.5 * ATR_14; high_to_low: VWAP touch (mean reversion)
members.exit_stop: low_to_high: 0.7 * ATR_14; high_to_low: 0.4 * ATR_14 beyond VWAP
filters: India_VIX < 25; extreme VIX makes HMM state estimates noisy
weaknesses: HMM is a parametric model that assumes Gaussian emissions; 1-min return distributions have fat tails, violating this assumption and causing state misclassification at extremes
Real-time HMM state estimation is computationally expensive (forward algorithm on 120 observations per bar); latency may cause missed entries on fast regime transitions
HMM with 2 states may be too simplistic — 3 states (low, medium, high vol) might better capture the intraday vol structure but adds model complexity and overfitting risk
members.prior_art: Hamilton (1989) regime-switching models; Bulla & Bulla (2006) HMM for financial time series. Nystrup et al. (2017) on HMM-based portfolio optimization.

members.name: hmm_regime_v1
members.thesis: Financial markets exhibit latent states (trending, mean-reverting, volatile-choppy) that are not directly observable but can be inferred from observable quantities (returns, volume, spread) using a Hidden Markov Model. By fitting a 3-state HMM on the previous session's 1-min data (observations: retu
entry_long: STATE_1 (trending): HMM_State == 1 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND EMA(close,9) > EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
STATE_2 (mean-reverting): HMM_State == 2 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND close < BB_lower
entry_short: STATE_1 (trending): HMM_State == 1 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND EMA(close,9) < EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
STATE_2 (mean-reverting): HMM_State == 2 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND close > BB_upper
members.exit_target: STATE_1: 50 bps; STATE_2: close reverts to BB_mid
filters: India VIX < 25; if VIX > 20, require State_Prob > 0.80 for entry
None — HMM handles regime detection internally
weaknesses: HMM fitted on previous session's data assumes stationarity of state dynamics across sessions — this breaks down during earnings season, macro events, or regime changes
3-state HMM is a strong modeling assumption — true market dynamics may have more states or non-Gaussian emissions; model misspecification leads to incorrect state decoding
Forward algorithm computation at each 1-min bar adds latency (O(N²) per bar where N=3 states); with many stocks this may exceed latency budget for real-time trading
members.prior_art: Bulla et al. (2011) on HMM for stock returns; Hamilton (1989) regime-switching models; Rydén et al. (1998) stylized facts and HMMs; hmmlearn library in Python widely available but intraday application
